pathway.title: Valaris Ltd — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Liquidity is the anchor. Valaris held cash of USD 525.1 million and an undrawn USD 375.0 million revolver at September 30, 2026, giving liquidity of USD 900.1 million. The only debt is USD 1,100.0 million of 8.375% second lien notes due April 30, 2030, and the revolver matures April 3, 2028 with nothing drawn. The notes' fair value of USD 1,125.2 million exceeded their principal, which does not point to market stress. - Earnings fell and then turned. Adjusted EBITDA, the company's own measure, was USD 642.2 million in FY2025 and USD 410.8 million over the last twelve months to Q3 2026, but USD 150.6 million in Q3 2026 against USD 96.5 million in Q2 2026. Gross leverage on principal moved from 1.71x to 2.68x and net leverage from 0.78x to 1.40x. The latest quarter is the strongest of the last four, so the last-twelve-months ratios overstate the current run rate, though the sources give no forecast. - Spending outruns cash flow. Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of USD 155.3 million did not cover capital expenditure of USD 328.0 million, and the 2026 capital expenditure guidance is USD 445.0 million to USD 470.0 million. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD -206.8 million over the last twelve months. The guidance describes maintenance and upgrade projects including contract-specific work, so part of the spending should earn revenue as rigs start work, but it is funded from cash until then. - The takeover is the main unknown. Transocean Ltd. will acquire Valaris by share exchange, with closing expected on or about December 1, 2026. The sources do not state whether closing triggers the notes' change-of-control repurchase offer at 101.0%, whether the notes and revolver stay in place, or what the combined capital structure is. Until closing, the agreement restricts new debt, dividends and repurchases. - Covenant headroom cannot be judged. The revolver carries minimum equity to total assets, minimum interest coverage and minimum liquidity tests with no printed level or reported figure. The company states only that it was in compliance in all material respects. - ARO is an off-balance-sheet claim on liquidity. Valaris holds notes receivable from ARO with a carrying value of USD 363.4 million that mature in 2027 and 2028 and are subordinated, and it may have to fund ARO newbuilds up to about USD 1.1 billion. ARO had cash of USD 32.1 million and has never paid a distribution. - Contracted revenue gives visibility but not certainty. Backlog was USD 4,750.1 million at November 2, 2026, concentrated in a few customers, and contracts can be terminated for convenience or if a customer fails to reach a final investment decision.

runs.text: - Strong liquidity relative to debt service (Documentary Fact; basis: liquidity of USD 900.1 million, cash and revolver figures in the financial base view). Mechanic: cash and an undrawn revolver cover the scheduled interest of about USD 92.1 million a year and 2026 capital spending shortfalls without market access. Implication: low near-term default risk on the standalone figures. - A short, simple maturity profile (Documentary Fact; basis: debt table and maturities in the financial base view). Mechanic: one note series, no principal before 2030, revolver undrawn. Implication: no principal falls due before 2030, ignoring the combination. - Contracted revenue visibility (Documentary Fact for backlog; Management Language for the outlook; basis: backlog and operating model rows in the business context). Mechanic: signed day rate contracts and rising drillship day rates support operating cash flow as idle rigs return to work. Implication: supports recovery of earnings, subject to termination rights. - Restrained shareholder behaviour (Documentary Fact; basis: governance rows). Mechanic: no dividends, no repurchases in 2026, and the combination agreement bars both until closing. Implication: no documented leakage of cash to shareholders.

- Negative free cash flow (Documentary Fact; basis: USD -206.8 million last twelve months, USD -172.7 million nine months 2026). Mechanic: upgrade spending is front-loaded against revenue. Implication: cash declined from USD 599.4 million to USD 525.1 million, so the liquidity cushion is being used. - Earnings trough and idle capacity (Documentary Fact; basis: Adjusted EBITDA and utilization figures). Mechanic: floater utilization of 58% in Q3 2026 means rigs carry cost without revenue. Implication: leverage of 2.68x is above the FY2025 level of 1.71x and sensitive to timing of contract starts. - Customer concentration and contract terms (Documentary Fact; basis: customer and contract rows). Mechanic: five customers were 49% of FY2025 revenues and some contracts can be ended for convenience. Implication: a single loss would reduce the visibility that supports leverage. - ARO exposure (Documentary Fact; basis: ARO rows). Mechanic: subordinated notes receivable, newbuild funding commitment and ARO's low cash. Implication: a contingent call on cash outside the debt figure. - Transaction uncertainty (Insufficient Information on creditor terms; basis: transaction rows). Mechanic: change-of-control terms, covenant tests and capital structure after closing are not supplied. Implication: the standalone view may be superseded; this limits confidence to Medium. - Covenant and ratings opacity (Insufficient Information; basis: covenant gap). Mechanic: levels, definitions and ratings are not supplied. Implication: availability of the revolver under stress cannot be tested.

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The one transaction in the sources is the pending business combination with Transocean Ltd., a Swiss corporation. The Business Combination Agreement was entered into on February 9, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:11). Transocean will acquire all issued and outstanding common shares of Valaris in exchange for Transocean shares at an exchange ratio of 15.235 Transocean shares for each Valaris share, by a court-approved scheme of arrangement under section 99 of the Companies Act 1981 of Bermuda (10-K page:8). Outstanding warrants will be assumed by Transocean and remain exercisable for the Fundamental Transaction Consideration as defined in the Warrant Agreement dated April 30, 2021 (10-Q Q3 page:11). On a fully diluted basis assuming conversion of Transocean's exchangeable bonds due 2029, Transocean shareholders would own approximately 53% and Valaris shareholders 47% of the combined company (10-Q Q3 page:11). The type is a stock-for-stock acquisition of Valaris. There is no sponsor, no cash consideration and no use of proceeds in the sources.

Status. Closing is subject to Valaris and Transocean shareholder approvals, a Bermuda sanction order, NYSE listing of the new Transocean shares, regulatory approvals or expiry of waiting periods, no legal prohibition, and the absence of a material adverse effect (10-Q Q3 page:12). Shareholder meetings for both companies are scheduled for November 24, 2026 and the Bermuda sanction hearing for November 26, 2026; closing is expected on or about December 1, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:12; Q3 release page:1). Management states that the combination "has received the required regulatory approvals" (Q3 release page:1). These dates are expectations at the cutoff; no document dated after November 3, 2026 is supplied.

Terms that matter to creditors. A termination fee of $173.0 million is payable by Valaris in specified circumstances; if Valaris shareholders fail to approve and that fee is not otherwise payable, Valaris must reimburse Transocean's transaction expenses up to $58 million (10-K page:22). Either party may terminate if the effective time has not occurred by February 9, 2027, subject to extension (10-K page:22). Valaris is restricted from soliciting alternative proposals and cannot terminate to accept a superior proposal (10-K page:23). Interim covenants restrict amending organizational documents, declaring dividends or repurchasing shares, encumbering assets, acquisitions and dispositions, incurring or guaranteeing indebtedness, and entering or amending material contracts (10-K page:24). Merger and integration expenses were 15.5 in Q3 2026 and 40.5 for nine months 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:12), per the financial base view.

Effect on debt: Not supplied. A search of all seven sources for refinancing, assumption of debt, and the Indenture's change-of-control provision found only the Indenture's 101.0% repurchase offer on a Change of Control Triggering Event (10-K page:127, as set out in the financial base view). No source states whether that event occurs on closing, whether the notes or revolver are repaid, assumed or amended, or what Transocean's own capital structure is. Transocean's financial statements and the Business Combination Agreement itself are not supplied. A creditor therefore cannot size the post-closing leverage, and the standalone figures are the only quantified base.

New debt issues. No new debt was issued in FY2025 or the first nine months of 2026: the cash flow statements show no debt issuance, and the only financing flows are share repurchases in 2025, tax withholdings and a small other item in 2026 (10-K page:107; 10-Q Q3 page:10). The outstanding notes were issued in 2023 and are described in the financial base view. Subsequent events after September 30, 2026 are limited to what the Q3 release and the 10-Q state: the start of the VALARIS DS-18 contract and the shareholder and court dates above.

Together they support a reported financial foundation, a last-twelve-months view from the Q3 release's discrete quarters, and a debt and liquidity description of a capital structure that has one note series and one undrawn revolver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strongest contrary evidence: the pending Business Combination (10-Q Q3 page:11 to page:12) can change ownership, covenant treatment and the debt structure. The 10-K (page:127) says that on a "Change of Control Triggering Event" the issuers "may be required to make an offer to repurchase" the notes at "101.0%" of principal. The supplied set does not say whether that event is triggered by the Transocean transaction. It also does not give the combination financing, Transocean's capital structure or the post-closing group.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Source risk mechanism: the revolver's "financial covenants that require us to maintain (i) a minimum book value of equity to total assets ratio, (ii) a minimum interest coverage ratio and (iii) a minimum amount of liquidity" (10-K page:129) carry no printed level, so a consumer cannot compute headroom and must not infer a pass from the statement that the company is "in compliance in all material respects". Compliance is a management assertion in a filing, not a tested ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Second mechanism: ARO is outside consolidated debt and earnings. Valaris reports notes receivable from ARO, an investment, lease receivables and payables, a contingent funding commitment for newbuild jackups, and ARO's own revolver and term loan (10-Q Q3 page:54 to page:56). A consumer that reads only consolidated debt omits an exposure that can call on Valaris cash. ARO's statements are not supplied, so the exposure can be described from Valaris's disclosure only.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Third mechanism: letters of credit and surety bonds sit outside the revolver. The Q3 10-Q (page:26) says none "were issued under the 2028 Credit Agreement". Revolver availability therefore must not be reduced for them without evidence, and must not be assumed unaffected by other conditions on borrowing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Valaris is a Bermuda-incorporated offshore drilling contractor with a fleet of 41 rigs at September 30, 2026: 13 drillships, 21 jackups and 7 jackups leased to ARO. It earns fixed day rates under contracts that customers can terminate in specified circumstances. The credit case rests on contracted deepwater drillship work with a small number of large customers, and on a capital structure of one note series and an undrawn revolver, described in the financial base view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The central transaction is the pending acquisition of Valaris by Transocean Ltd. under a Business Combination Agreement dated February 9, 2026. It is a share exchange at 15.235 Transocean shares for each Valaris share, implemented by a Bermuda court-approved scheme of arrangement, and no cash consideration is described. Valaris shareholders would own about 47% of the combined company on a fully diluted basis assuming conversion of Transocean's exchangeable bonds due 2029. Shareholder meetings are set for November 24, 2026, a court hearing for November 26, 2026, and closing is expected on or about December 1, 2026. These are expectations, not completed events. For a creditor the important point is what the sources do not say: no supplied document states whether the combination triggers the change-of-control offer in the Indenture, whether the notes or revolver stay in place, or what the combined capital structure is. Until closing, the agreement restricts dividends, share repurchases, asset encumbrance, acquisitions and dispositions, and new or guaranteed debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business view is otherwise stable to improving on management's account, with specific exposures: customer concentration, termination and FID-contingency rights in contracts, Middle East operations, and ARO funding. The view is Medium confidence. The facts are documentary, but the effect of the combination on creditors is not assessable from the supplied sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The one transaction in the sources is the pending business combination with Transocean Ltd., a Swiss corporation. The Business Combination Agreement was entered into on February 9, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:11). Transocean will acquire all issued and outstanding common shares of Valaris in exchange for Transocean shares at an exchange ratio of 15.235 Transocean shares for each Valaris share, by a court-approved scheme of arrangement under section 99 of the Companies Act 1981 of Bermuda (10-K page:8). Outstanding warrants will be assumed by Transocean and remain exercisable for the Fundamental Transaction Consideration as defined in the Warrant Agreement dated April 30, 2021 (10-Q Q3 page:11). On a fully diluted basis assuming conversion of Transocean's exchangeable bonds due 2029, Transocean shareholders would own approximately 53% and Valaris shareholders 47% of the combined company (10-Q Q3 page:11). The type is a stock-for-stock acquisition of Valaris. There is no sponsor, no cash consideration and no use of proceeds in the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Status. Closing is subject to Valaris and Transocean shareholder approvals, a Bermuda sanction order, NYSE listing of the new Transocean shares, regulatory approvals or expiry of waiting periods, no legal prohibition, and the absence of a material adverse effect (10-Q Q3 page:12). Shareholder meetings for both companies are scheduled for November 24, 2026 and the Bermuda sanction hearing for November 26, 2026; closing is expected on or about December 1, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:12; Q3 release page:1). Management states that the combination "has received the required regulatory approvals" (Q3 release page:1). These dates are expectations at the cutoff; no document dated after November 3, 2026 is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Terms that matter to creditors. A termination fee of $173.0 million is payable by Valaris in specified circumstances; if Valaris shareholders fail to approve and that fee is not otherwise payable, Valaris must reimburse Transocean's transaction expenses up to $58 million (10-K page:22). Either party may terminate if the effective time has not occurred by February 9, 2027, subject to extension (10-K page:22). Valaris is restricted from soliciting alternative proposals and cannot terminate to accept a superior proposal (10-K page:23). Interim covenants restrict amending organizational documents, declaring dividends or repurchasing shares, encumbering assets, acquisitions and dispositions, incurring or guaranteeing indebtedness, and entering or amending material contracts (10-K page:24). Merger and integration expenses were 15.5 in Q3 2026 and 40.5 for nine months 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:12), per the financial base view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Effect on debt: Not supplied. A search of all seven sources for refinancing, assumption of debt, and the Indenture's change-of-control provision found only the Indenture's 101.0% repurchase offer on a Change of Control Triggering Event (10-K page:127, as set out in the financial base view). No source states whether that event occurs on closing, whether the notes or revolver are repaid, assumed or amended, or what Transocean's own capital structure is. Transocean's financial statements and the Business Combination Agreement itself are not supplied. A creditor therefore cannot size the post-closing leverage, and the standalone figures are the only quantified base.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt issues. No new debt was issued in FY2025 or the first nine months of 2026: the cash flow statements show no debt issuance, and the only financing flows are share repurchases in 2025, tax withholdings and a small other item in 2026 (10-K page:107; 10-Q Q3 page:10). The outstanding notes were issued in 2023 and are described in the financial base view. Subsequent events after September 30, 2026 are limited to what the Q3 release and the 10-Q state: the start of the VALARIS DS-18 contract and the shareholder and court dates above.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue durability. Evidence: backlog of 4,750.1 at November 2, 2026 against 4,672.3 at February 17, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:35), with contracts that may be terminated for convenience or lack of FID (10-K page:10). Mechanic: contracted day rates give revenue visibility for debt service, but termination rights and the FID contingency make part of the backlog conditional. Implication: contracted revenue supports near-term liquidity while the notes do not mature before 2030; the conditionality argues against treating backlog as committed cash. Counter-evidence: none logged; the backlog by year at November 2, 2026 is Not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margin and cash flow risk. Evidence: drillship average daily revenue rose to $469,000 in Q3 2026 while floater utilization was 58% (Q3 release page:12), and capital expenditure above operating cash flow in 2026 per the financial base view. Mechanic: idle or stacked rigs carry fixed cost, and contract-specific upgrades precede revenue. Implication: improving drillship contracting should lift cash flow, but liquidity depends on those rigs starting work on schedule.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Concentration. Evidence: five customers at 49% of FY2025 revenues and 11 rigs on national oil company contracts (10-K page:11, page:45). Mechanic: loss or renegotiation of one contract is material, and national oil company terms can be non-negotiable. Implication: tail risk on any single contract; no customer credit assessment is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Transaction and creditor control. Evidence: the stock-for-stock combination, the Indenture's change-of-control offer at 101.0%, and the silence of the sources on debt treatment. Mechanic: closing could trigger noteholder rights or change covenant tests, and interim covenants limit new debt until closing. Implication: standalone credit metrics may not describe the issuer after December 1, 2026. This is the key uncertainty.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - ARO. Evidence: notes receivable, newbuild funding commitment, and ARO's thin cash against rising newbuild orders (10-Q Q3 page:54 to page:56). Mechanic: an unconsolidated affiliate can draw on Valaris cash without appearing in debt. Implication: contingent liquidity use; the commitment is a maximum, not an expected call.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor, no dividends, no repurchases in 2026. Mechanic: no extraction channel is documented. Implication: neutral; behaviour after closing is Not supplied.

fields.value: Credit synthesis for Valaris Ltd, issuer id `val`, as of 2026-11-05 (cutoff 2026-11-05), pathway `credit_snapshot`, reporting currency USD. Scope is the fundamental credit view built from the financial base view (CP-1) and the business and transaction context (CP-1A) on a standalone basis, with the pending Transocean combination treated as a transaction risk. No peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion is given.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The conclusions rest on the upstream handoffs. The source files were used only for the two supplementary checks marked in the calculations. Locators in the evidence trace are `page:N` chunks of the pinned files, not printed pages.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Valaris Ltd has a low standalone refinancing risk and moderate leverage, but its credit quality now depends on a takeover whose effect on creditors is not disclosed. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 900.1 million and no debt principal due before 2030. The weakest point is cash generation: over the last twelve months Adjusted EBITDA of USD 410.8 million was below capital expenditure of USD 434.3 million, and cash fell. Three things decide the outcome: whether idle drillships keep returning to work at higher day rates, how the combination treats the USD 1,100.0 million of notes, and whether ARO draws on Valaris cash. Confidence is Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Liquidity is the anchor. Valaris held cash of USD 525.1 million and an undrawn USD 375.0 million revolver at September 30, 2026, giving liquidity of USD 900.1 million. The only debt is USD 1,100.0 million of 8.375% second lien notes due April 30, 2030, and the revolver matures April 3, 2028 with nothing drawn. The notes' fair value of USD 1,125.2 million exceeded their principal, which does not point to market stress.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings fell and then turned. Adjusted EBITDA, the company's own measure, was USD 642.2 million in FY2025 and USD 410.8 million over the last twelve months to Q3 2026, but USD 150.6 million in Q3 2026 against USD 96.5 million in Q2 2026. Gross leverage on principal moved from 1.71x to 2.68x and net leverage from 0.78x to 1.40x. The latest quarter is the strongest of the last four, so the last-twelve-months ratios overstate the current run rate, though the sources give no forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Spending outruns cash flow. Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of USD 155.3 million did not cover capital expenditure of USD 328.0 million, and the 2026 capital expenditure guidance is USD 445.0 million to USD 470.0 million. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was USD -206.8 million over the last twelve months. The guidance describes maintenance and upgrade projects including contract-specific work, so part of the spending should earn revenue as rigs start work, but it is funded from cash until then.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The takeover is the main unknown. Transocean Ltd. will acquire Valaris by share exchange, with closing expected on or about December 1, 2026. The sources do not state whether closing triggers the notes' change-of-control repurchase offer at 101.0%, whether the notes and revolver stay in place, or what the combined capital structure is. Until closing, the agreement restricts new debt, dividends and repurchases.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant headroom cannot be judged. The revolver carries minimum equity to total assets, minimum interest coverage and minimum liquidity tests with no printed level or reported figure. The company states only that it was in compliance in all material respects.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - ARO is an off-balance-sheet claim on liquidity. Valaris holds notes receivable from ARO with a carrying value of USD 363.4 million that mature in 2027 and 2028 and are subordinated, and it may have to fund ARO newbuilds up to about USD 1.1 billion. ARO had cash of USD 32.1 million and has never paid a distribution.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Contracted revenue gives visibility but not certainty. Backlog was USD 4,750.1 million at November 2, 2026, concentrated in a few customers, and contracts can be terminated for convenience or if a customer fails to reach a final investment decision.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strong liquidity relative to debt service (Documentary Fact; basis: liquidity of USD 900.1 million, cash and revolver figures in the financial base view). Mechanic: cash and an undrawn revolver cover the scheduled interest of about USD 92.1 million a year and 2026 capital spending shortfalls without market access. Implication: low near-term default risk on the standalone figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - A short, simple maturity profile (Documentary Fact; basis: debt table and maturities in the financial base view). Mechanic: one note series, no principal before 2030, revolver undrawn. Implication: no principal falls due before 2030, ignoring the combination.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Contracted revenue visibility (Documentary Fact for backlog; Management Language for the outlook; basis: backlog and operating model rows in the business context). Mechanic: signed day rate contracts and rising drillship day rates support operating cash flow as idle rigs return to work. Implication: supports recovery of earnings, subject to termination rights.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Restrained shareholder behaviour (Documentary Fact; basis: governance rows). Mechanic: no dividends, no repurchases in 2026, and the combination agreement bars both until closing. Implication: no documented leakage of cash to shareholders.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Negative free cash flow (Documentary Fact; basis: USD -206.8 million last twelve months, USD -172.7 million nine months 2026). Mechanic: upgrade spending is front-loaded against revenue. Implication: cash declined from USD 599.4 million to USD 525.1 million, so the liquidity cushion is being used.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings trough and idle capacity (Documentary Fact; basis: Adjusted EBITDA and utilization figures). Mechanic: floater utilization of 58% in Q3 2026 means rigs carry cost without revenue. Implication: leverage of 2.68x is above the FY2025 level of 1.71x and sensitive to timing of contract starts.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Customer concentration and contract terms (Documentary Fact; basis: customer and contract rows). Mechanic: five customers were 49% of FY2025 revenues and some contracts can be ended for convenience. Implication: a single loss would reduce the visibility that supports leverage.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - ARO exposure (Documentary Fact; basis: ARO rows). Mechanic: subordinated notes receivable, newbuild funding commitment and ARO's low cash. Implication: a contingent call on cash outside the debt figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Transaction uncertainty (Insufficient Information on creditor terms; basis: transaction rows). Mechanic: change-of-control terms, covenant tests and capital structure after closing are not supplied. Implication: the standalone view may be superseded; this limits confidence to Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant and ratings opacity (Insufficient Information; basis: covenant gap). Mechanic: levels, definitions and ratings are not supplied. Implication: availability of the revolver under stress cannot be tested.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Valaris Ltd can service its debt from cash and an undrawn revolver while its drillship fleet returns to work at higher day rates, but the pending Transocean combination and ARO funding obligations mean creditors cannot rely on the standalone figures alone.

Scheduled October 30, 2026 coupon: 1,100.0 x 8.375% / 2 = 46.1 (from the financial base view). Outlay = 117.0 + 46.1 = 163.1 to 142.0 + 46.1 = 188.1. Cash after these outlays and with no operating cash flow, asset sale proceeds or merger costs: 525.1 - 163.1 = 362.0 to 525.1 - 188.1 = 337.0. Adding the undrawn revolver: 362.0 + 375.0 = 737.0 to 337.0 + 375.0 = 712.0. Q3 2026 operating cash flow was 67.2, which is excluded here. Whether the coupon was paid is not stated in the sources.
